title: Light and Darkness
lead: From the first words of creation, "Let there be light" (Genesis 1:3), the Bible uses light and darkness for God and his absence, truth and falsehood, good and evil, life and death. The prophets promise that the LORD will be his people's light; John's Gospel and letters build on the picture ("God is light", 1 John 1:5; "I am the light of the world", John 8:12), and the Dead Sea Scrolls divide humanity into "the sons of light" and "the sons of darkness" (Community Rule, column 1, lines 9-10, in Vermes's translation).

sections.b: God creates light and separates it from darkness (Genesis 1:3-5). The plague of darkness falls on Egypt while Israel has light (Exodus 10:21-23). The psalmist says "The LORD is my light" (Psalm 27:1), and Isaiah sees a people walking in darkness who have seen a great light (Isaiah 9:2) and a day when the LORD himself will be his people's light (Isaiah 60:19-20). In the New Testament Jesus calls himself the light of the world (John 8:12) and his disciples the light of the world (Matthew 5:14); Paul calls believers "children of light" (Ephesians 5:8; 1 Thessalonians 5:5). The new Jerusalem needs no sun, for God's glory is its light (Revelation 21:23).
